biography.plain_text: A.W. Flitton was a Pretoria businessman and South African sailing administrator who became president of the national sailing association. After serving as a wartime aircraft mechanic, he and F.C. Alderson used their military gratuities to start a business. He also won the Dewar Shield twice as a competitive sailor.

long_biography.plain_text:
A.W. Flitton helped establish organised sailing at Hartbeespoort Dam as its reservoir first filled. He attended the initial meeting at Pretoria's Grand Hotel in 1923, before the group formally named and organised its sailing club. Among the club's early craft, his used a Bermudan rig when that arrangement was still a novelty.

His contribution also involved work ashore. He built walls, steps and rockeries around the clubhouse and donated a block of bedrooms for members. In later years he followed sailor Dick Richards at regattas, watching his tactics and quietly pointing out mistakes afterwards.
